title: Refine copy-paste layout preservation and selection micro-gestures across density transitions for virtual table
creator: Arielle Park
description:
Problem: When users switch density modes (compact/regular/comfortable) in virtualized tables, we see two classes of issues: 1) copy-paste of multi-cell selections loses intended layout (column widths or collapsed columns), and 2) selection micro-gestures (drag-to-select, double-click-to-select-cell) feel inconsistent across density transitions and during progressive row mounting. This creates friction for power users who rely on keyboard + mouse flows and for assistive tech users where selection state must be predictable.

Goal: Define a cohesive behavior spec and interaction patterns so that: (a) copy/paste preserves logical table layout and cell context across density changes and between machines/OSes; (b) selection gestures remain stable during virtualization (no surprise selection jumps when rows mount/unmount); (c) affordances communicate state during density animations (visual previews, ghost overlays).

Non-goals: Not addressing backend CSV export format or per-user clipboard encryption. Not changing fundamental virtualization strategy (we'll work with engineering's existing progressive-mount runtime).

Stakeholders: Design System, Table Component owners (ENG: Nora Chen), Accessibility lead (Matt Rivera), Product PM for Console (Rina Patel), QA (Samir Khan).

Deliverables:
- Interaction spec with edge-case flows and acceptance criteria (this ticket).
- Figma prototypes: single-row, multi-row copy/paste, selection drag in all three density modes.
- Accessibility notes and ARIA patterns for selection announcements.
- Small dev-friendly handoff with CSS token suggestions and a micro-feature flag for progressive rollout.

Acceptance criteria (must pass):
1) Copy/paste: Pasting a rectangular selection into another app or into a new table preserves visual column order and cell separators in at least two major hosts (Slack and Sheets) in our internal QA matrix; behavior documented.
2) Selection stability: Drag-select operations do not lose the selection anchor when virtualization causes row mounts/unmounts. Reproduction steps and unit test cases are listed.
3) Density transition preview: When switching density while a selection exists, UI shows a lightweight preview overlay (ghost frames) for 300ms before committing layout; prototype and token guidance attached.
4) Accessibility: Screen reader announces selection range changes and density change previews in a non-noisy way (one concise announcement).

Design decisions and trade-offs considered: 
- We will favor a logical-selection model (based on column keys + row ids) over pixel-based selection to ensure copy/paste portability. Trade-off: requires stable row ids propagated to clipboard metadata for rich pastes (we'll degrade to plain-text CSV when host doesn't honor metadata).
- Preview overlay is cosmetic and time-bound (300ms) to avoid blocking interactions; trade-off is momentary visual duplication — chosen to reduce surprise when density quantization alters column widths.
- For virtualization stability, we avoid expanding the visible buffer too far (cost) and instead rely on selection anchoring + deterministic mount order so selection logic can rehydrate; engineering will add a lightweight selection-controller hook.

Implementation notes for engineers: 
- Clipboard payload: include a small JSON mime-type entry (e.g., application/x-redwood-table-selection) with row ids, col keys, and column widths; fallback to text/csv. Documented in the spec.
- Selection anchor model: maintain {anchorRowId, anchorColKey, focusRowId, focusColKey} in component state that survives re-renders and virtualization window shifts.
- Visual preview: CSS variables (tokens) for preview opacity and border radius: --table-density-preview-opacity, --table-density-preview-duration. Provide token default values in the handoff.

Risks: 
- Some external paste targets will ignore custom clipboard mime types — fallback will produce plain text. 
- Adding clipboard metadata increases surface area for privacy review; flagging security_review_required.

References and artifacts:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/Redwood-Table-Density-Selection-Exploration (prototype frames: copy-paste, drag-select)
- Engineering spike notes: https://drive.redwoodcompany.com/drive/folders/table-virt-spike-2026
- Proposed PR (staging): https://github.com/redwood-inference/core-ui/pull/9123 (WIP, includes selection-controller hook API)

Next steps (this ticket):
1) Finalize prototype frames for drag-select + density-change preview (Design) — due 2026-03-12.
2) Sync with ENG on selection-controller API and minimal clipboard mime support — sync meeting scheduled 2026-03-13.
3) Produce accessibility announcement wording and ARIA snippet — pending ARIA review.

Notes: This ticket intentionally keeps scope limited so dev effort is a small incremental change to the table component library rather than a full rework of virtualization strategy.
